title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
slides: Can ChatGPT now spend your money without asking?
A new Wallet feature lets agents complete checkouts
But the agent pauses for approval on every purchase
You set spending limits and merchant allowlists first
Test it with one low-stakes purchase this week
thread_text:
1. Can ChatGPT spend your money?

A new Wallet feature lets AI agents complete checkouts. The agent pauses for approval on every purchase, so you stay in control.

2. Approval on every purchase

The agent won't finalize a transaction without your explicit sign-off. That means no surprise charges, but also a manual step each time.

3. Set limits first

Before any purchase, you define spending limits and merchant allowlists. The agent can only act within those boundaries.

4. Test with a small buy

Try one low-stakes purchase this week. See how the approval flow works and whether the limits feel right for you.

5. Would you trust it?

If the agent asks for approval on every checkout, does it save time or add friction? Test it on a real low-stakes purchase and decide.

instagram.caption:
ChatGPT now has a Wallet that can complete checkouts for you — but the agent stops for approval on every single purchase before anything is charged.

You set spending limits and a merchant allowlist first, so the agent only acts inside boundaries you define.

That means no surprise charges, but also a manual sign-off each time it buys something. 🔒

If you publish or create content, this changes how you'd test AI tools for real tasks: one low-stakes purchase shows whether the approval flow saves time or just adds friction to your day.

Would you hand checkout to an agent that pauses for your approval every time, or does that defeat the point? 💳🤖
